narrative_purpose: Makes the first killer visible: with the outside air thick in carbon dioxide, the gas the body normally exhales floods backward into the blood, turning it acid.
subject: A painterly close cross-section of a single lung air sac (alveolus) wrapped in fine blood capillaries. Instead of carbon-dioxide motes leaving the blood, dense streams of amber motes pour the wrong way - inward, from the crowded air space into the capillaries - and the blood flushes from healthy red toward an angry acidic orange where they enter.
scene: An intimate biological micro-scene, the air space crowded and amber-heavy on one side, the capillary network on the other, the reversed inward flood the dramatic centre.
camera: Extreme close anatomical view, shallow depth, the membrane between air and blood across the middle of the frame.
light: Soft internal glow; the amber air space warm and oppressive, the blood lit from within, brightening to a hot acidic orange at the flood front.
palette: Amber-heavy air space, deep red blood shifting to acidic orange, cool teal-indigo surround to keep it within the chapter's palette.
style: Painterly speculative-anatomy plate, hand-painted, organic texture, NOT a clinical textbook diagram and NOT a 3D render.
detail_level: Crisp on the membrane and the reversed inward flood; softer capillary network behind.
composition: Air space upper, capillaries lower, the inward amber flood crossing the central membrane line; no drawn arrows or labels - the direction reads from the motion of the motes.
consistency_notes: Amber motes are the chapter's consistent visual for carbon dioxide. Reads as a painted micro-scene, not a medical schematic.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no chemical formulae, no schematic chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
